questions.question: A fast train takes 1 hour less than a slow train for a journey of 96 km. If the speed of the slow train is 8 km/h less than that of the fast train, then find the speeds of the fast train and slow train respectively
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct formula for speed difference: **Distance** = [Product of Speeds ÷ Difference of Speeds] × **Time Difference**.

96 = [S₁ × S₂ ÷ 8] × 1 ⇒ S₁ × S₂ = 96 × 8 = 768.

From the given options, only 32 × 24 = 768 and the difference 32 − 24 = 8 km/h satisfies the condition.

Hence, the speeds are 32 km/h and 24 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 32 km/h, 24 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Distance = 96 km

Time Difference (ΔT) = 1 hour

Speed Difference = 8 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96a1ff0714e13014d326b3392ca87e2c1011577be712c9b9d9c3c57433cada11.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the **fast train** be x km/h.

Then, the speed of the **slow train** is (x − 8) km/h.

⇒ 96/(x − 8) − 96/x = 1

⇒ 96[ (x − (x − 8)) / (x(x − 8)) ] = 1

⇒ 96 × 8 = x² − 8x

⇒ x² − 8x − 768 = 0

⇒ x² − 32x + 24x − 768 = 0

⇒ x(x − 32) + 24(x − 32) = 0

⇒ (x − 32)(x + 24) = 0

⇒ x = 32 (Speed cannot be negative, so x ≠ −24)

Speed of **fast train** = 32 km/h

Speed of **slow train** = 32 − 8 = 24 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 32 km/h, 24 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relation

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If speed increases, time decreases.

Quadratic Shortcut

In equations like x² − Sx + P = 0, the sum of roots is S and the product is P. In speed problems, the positive root is the answer.

Average Speed

If a journey is covered at two different speeds x and y for equal distances, the average speed is (2xy) ÷ (x + y).</p

questions.question: A person got an article at 22% discount, if he got no discount, then he had to pay ₹1,760 more. How much did he pay (in ₹) for the article?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The extra amount to be paid without a **discount** represents the discount value itself.

Given: 22% **Discount** = ₹1,760

Unitary Value: 1% = 1760 ÷ 22 = ₹80

The person paid (100% − 22%) = 78% of the **Marked Price**.

Total amount paid = 78 × 80 = ₹6,240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,240.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Discount Percentage** = 22%

Difference between **Marked Price** and **Selling Price** (Discount Value) = ₹1,760

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08e4f3dc201c42df3ed5681c66174ce48ac17ba48b0769731e3ddd0966a78ec3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Marked Price** of the article be ₹X.

⇒ **Discount** = 22% of X = ₹1,760

⇒ (22 ÷ 100) × X = 1760

⇒ X = (1760 × 100) ÷ 22

⇒ X = 80 × 100 = ₹8,000

⇒ **Selling Price** = **Marked Price** − **Discount**

⇒ **Selling Price** = 8000 − 1760 = ₹6,240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,240.**

**__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) and Selling Price (SP)

The **Marked Price** is the price printed on the label. **Selling Price** is the price after applying **discounts**: SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Relationship between MP and CP

If a profit P% is made after a discount D%, then MP ÷ CP = (100 + P) ÷ (100 − D).

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − [a × b ÷ 100])%.

questions.question: 360 toffees are distributed among Pushkal, Quadir and Rustam in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. After distribution, Quadir gives 20% of his toffees to Pushkal and Rustam gives 25% of his toffees to Pushkal. What is the new ratio of toffees with Pushkal, Quadir and Rustam?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total ratio units = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 units → 360 toffees. So, 1 unit = 40.

Initial: **Pushkal** = 80, **Quadir** = 120, **Rustam** = 160.

**Quadir** gives 20% of 120 = 24; **Rustam** gives 25% of 160 = 40.

New counts: **Pushkal** = 80 + 24 + 40 = 144, **Quadir** = 120 − 24 = 96, **Rustam** = 160 − 40 = 120.

New Ratio = 144 : 96 : 120 = 6 : 4 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 : 4 : 5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **toffees** = 360

Initial distribution ratio (**Pushkal** : **Quadir** : **Rustam**) = 2 : 3 : 4

**Formula Used:**

Individual share = (Individual ratio / Sum of ratios) × Total value

Percentage value = (Percentage / 100) × Total quantity

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fecc6abdb417bef27413c7700da8c82a567fb042f9eb1ac6f8167ea83f7631e8.png] 

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9

⇒ **Pushkal** (Initial) = (2/9) × 360 = 80

⇒ **Quadir** (Initial) = (3/9) × 360 = 120

⇒ **Rustam** (Initial) = (4/9) × 360 = 160

⇒ **Toffees** from **Quadir** = 20% of 120 = 0.20 × 120 = 24

⇒ **Toffees** from **Rustam** = 25% of 160 = 0.25 × 160 = 40

⇒ New **Pushkal** = 80 + 24 + 40 = 144

⇒ New **Quadir** = 120 − 24 = 96

⇒ New **Rustam** = 160 − 40 = 120

⇒ New Ratio = 144 : 96 : 120

⇒ Divide all by 24 (HCF): 6 : 4 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is 6 : 4 : 5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio Distribution Rule

To divide a quantity N into a ratio a : b : c, the parts are calculated as N × a/(a+b+c), N × b/(a+b+c), and N × c/(a+b+c).

Simplifying Ratios

A ratio a : b : c can be simplified by dividing each term by their Highest Common Factor (HCF) to reach its simplest form.

Percentage of a Quantity

x% of a value y is calculated as (x/100) × y. In transfers, this amount is subtracted from the source and added to the recipient.</p

questions.question: The HCF of 513, 1134 and 1215 is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **HCF** of numbers is always a factor of the **difference** between any two of those numbers.

Difference between 1215 and 1134 = 81.

Difference between 1134 and 513 = 621.

The **HCF** must be a factor of the smallest difference, which is 81.

Among the given options, only **27** is a factor of 81 (81 ÷ 27 = 3).

Checking 27 for all numbers: 513 ÷ 27 = 19, 1134 ÷ 27 = 42, 1215 ÷ 27 = 45.

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three numbers 513, 1134, and 1215.

**Method:** **Prime Factorization Method**

⇒ 513 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 19 = 3³ × 19

⇒ 1134 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 7 = 2 × 3⁴ × 7

⇒ 1215 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 3⁵ × 5

⇒ To find the **HCF**, identify the common prime factors and take the **lowest power** of each.

⇒ The common prime factor for all three numbers is 3.

⇒ The lowest power of 3 present in all terms is 3³.

⇒ HCF = 3³ = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The **HCF** (also known as GCD) is the largest positive integer that divides each of the integers without leaving a remainder.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b', the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Division Method for HCF

To find HCF of large numbers, divide the larger number by the smaller one and then divide the previous divisor by the remainder until the remainder becomes zero. The last divisor is the **HCF**.</p

questions.question:
Two masses of 1 kg and 2 kg were dropped from a height of 3.2 metres. Their respective velocities just before touching the ground will be:

(Assume acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8 m/s for both**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The velocities of objects falling freely under gravity are independent of their masses.
 
• Both the 1 kg and 2 kg masses will experience the same acceleration due to gravity (g = 10 m/s²).
 
• The velocity just before touching the ground is determined by the equation v = sqrt{2gh}, where g is the acceleration due to gravity and h is the height from which the object is dropped.
 
• Using the formula v = sqrt{2 times 10 times 3.2} = sqrt{64} = 8 {m/s}, both masses will have the same velocity just before hitting the ground.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity:**

 
 
• Gravity is a fundamental force that attracts objects towards the center of the Earth.
 
• The value of acceleration due to gravity near Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s² but is commonly approximated as 10 m/s² for simplicity in calculations.
 
• The value of gravity can vary depending on location, altitude, and Earth's irregular shape.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• When an object is dropped, and the only force acting on it is gravity, it is said to be in free fall.
 
• Objects in free fall accelerate at a constant rate due to gravity, regardless of their mass.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Velocity in Free Fall:**
 
 
• The velocity of an object just before hitting the ground can be found using the formula v = sqrt{2gh}, where g is the gravitational acceleration and h is the height.
 
• This equation assumes there is no air resistance.
 
 
 
• **Mass and Gravity:**
 
 
• In the absence of air resistance, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their mass. This was famously demonstrated by Galileo.

questions.question: The igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are interconvertible through a continuous process called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rock cycle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The rock cycle is a continuous process through which rocks are transformed from one type to another over geological time scales.
 
• It involves the formation, breakdown, and reformation of rocks due to various geological processes.
 
• Igneous rocks can be broken down into sediments that form sedimentary rocks, which can then be subjected to heat and pressure to become metamorphic rocks.
 
• Metamorphic rocks can melt to form magma, which cools to become igneous rocks, thus completing the cycle.
 
• The rock cycle is driven by Earth's internal heat, plate tectonics, and surface processes like weathering and erosion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Igneous Rocks**

 
 
• Formed from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.
 
• Examples include granite (intrusive) and basalt (extrusive).
 
 
 
• **Sedimentary Rocks**
 
 
• Formed from the accumulation and lithification of sediments.
 
• Examples include sandstone, limestone, and shale.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks**
 
 
• Formed from the alteration of existing rocks due to high heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids.
 
• Examples include marble (from limestone) and schist (from shale).
 
 
 
• **Weathering and Erosion**
 
 
• Weathering is the breakdown of rocks at Earth's surface due to atmospheric conditions.
 
• Erosion involves the removal and transportation of weathered material by natural agents like water, wind, and ice.

questions.question: 'Sange Meel Se Mulaqat' is the documentary of which famous musician?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bismillah Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bismillah Khan** was a renowned Indian musician credited with popularizing the shehnai, a traditional Indian wind instrument.
 
• The documentary **'Sange Meel Se Mulaqat'** focuses on the life and musical journey of Bismillah Khan.
 
• Bismillah Khan received India's highest civilian honors, including the **Bharat Ratna** in 2001.
 
• He performed at the Red Fort on India's first Independence Day in 1947, marking the beginning of a tradition.
 
• Bismillah Khan's contribution to Indian classical music is celebrated globally, and he is remembered as a cultural icon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shehnai**

 
 
• The shehnai is a double-reed instrument traditional to India, often used in auspicious occasions and classical music.
 
• It is similar to the oboe and is known for its rich and soulful sound.
 
• Bismillah Khan is credited with elevating the shehnai from a folk instrument to one of classical status.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Ratna**
 
 
• It is the highest civilian award in India, instituted in 1954.
 
• The award recognizes exceptional service towards the advancement of art, literature, and science, and in recognition of public service of the highest order.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music**
 
 
• It is divided into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian) music.
 
• Indian classical music is characterized by its raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic patterns).
 
• Prominent instruments include the sitar, tabla, and shehnai.
 
 
 
• **Independence Day Performance**
 
 
• Bismillah Khan's performance at the Red Fort on August 15, 1947, is a historic moment in Indian history.
 
• His shehnai rendition signified the dawn of India's independence from British rule.

questions.question: Who among the following adopted the policy of consolidation in place of expansion by eliminating the rebels?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ghiyasuddin Balban was the Sultan of Delhi from 1266 to 1287.
 
• He adopted a policy of consolidation by eliminating the rebels and maintaining strict control over his territories.
 
• Balban is known for his strong centralized administration and efforts to strengthen the Sultanate against internal and external threats.
 
• He implemented a policy of "blood and iron" to suppress revolts and rebellions, ensuring the stability and security of his rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shamsuddin Iltutmish**

 
 
• Iltutmish was the third Sultan of Delhi and a prominent ruler of the Mamluk dynasty.
 
• He is known for consolidating the Delhi Sultanate and introducing important administrative reforms.
 
• Iltutmish completed the construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi.
 
• He introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital, standardizing the monetary system of the Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Raziya**
 
 
• Raziya, also known as Razia Sultan, was the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• She ruled from 1236 to 1240 and was known for her administrative skills and efforts to promote gender equality.
 
• Raziya faced significant opposition from the nobility and was eventually overthrown.
 
 
 
• **Nasiruddin Mahmud**
 
 
• Nasiruddin Mahmud was the Sultan of Delhi from 1246 to 1266.
 
• He was a nominal ruler, with real power being held by his deputy, Ghiyasuddin Balban.
 
• Mahmud's reign is noted for the consolidation of the Sultanate's administration and military.
 
 
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban's Policies**
 
 
• Balban emphasized a strong and centralized administration to ensure the Sultanate's stability.
 
• He implemented a strict policy of law and order, using harsh measures to suppress rebellions and maintain control.
 
• Balban's reign marked the beginning of the consolidation of the Sultanate, setting the stage for future rulers.

questions.question: Which of the following types of emergencies is declared under Article 360 of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial Emergency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 360 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President of India to declare a Financial Emergency if they are satisfied that the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
• During a Financial Emergency, the executive authority of the Union extends to giving directions to any State to observe certain canons of financial propriety or such other directions as deemed necessary.
 
• Article 360 allows the President to reduce the salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving in the State and the Union.
 
• Under the Financial Emergency, the President can also reserve all money bills or other financial bills for their consideration after they are passed by the legislature of the State.
 
• No Financial Emergency has been declared in India so far.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Emergency (Article 352)**

 
 
• Declared on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• It results in a modification of the federal structure of India, leading to a centralization of power.
 
• During National Emergency, fundamental rights under Article 19 are automatically suspended, and other rights can also be suspended by a presidential order.
 
 
 
• **State Emergency (Article 356)**
 
 
• Also known as President's Rule, it can be proclaimed on the failure of constitutional machinery in a state.
 
• During President's Rule, the state legislature is either dissolved or suspended, and the state comes under the direct control of the central government.
 
• The Governor administers the state in the name of the President.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Emergency**
 
 
• It is another term used for State Emergency under Article 356.
 
• It occurs when a state government is unable to function according to the constitutional provisions.
 
• This provision has been used numerous times since independence.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Approval**
 
 
• A Financial Emergency must be approved by both houses of Parliament within two months of its declaration.
 
• If approved, it remains in force indefinitely until it is revoked by the President.
 
• The resolution approving the Financial Emergency needs to be passed by a simple majority.

• National Unity Day, also known as **Rashtriya Ekta Diwas**, is celebrated in India on **October 31** every year.
 
• This day commemorates the birth anniversary of **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, who played a key role in the unification of India.
 
• It was introduced by the Government of India in **2014** to honor Sardar Patel's contributions to national integration.
 
• Various events such as the **"Run for Unity"** are organized across the country to mark this occasion.
 
• The day emphasizes the importance of maintaining the country's unity and integrity.

• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**

 
 
• Also known as the **"Iron Man of India"**.
 
• First Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of independent India.
 
• Played a crucial role in the integration of over 500 princely states into the Indian Union.
 
• His efforts and strategies were pivotal in maintaining the nation's unity post-independence.
 
 
 
• **Statue of Unity**
 
 
• Located in the state of Gujarat, India.
 
• It is the world's tallest statue, standing at a height of 182 meters (597 feet).
 
• Dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and inaugurated on October 31, 2018.
 
• Symbolizes Patel's vision of a united India.
 
 
 
• **Run for Unity**
 
 
• An annual event organized on National Unity Day.
 
• Aims to promote national integration and communal harmony.
 
• Participants from various walks of life join to reinforce the message of unity.
 
 
 
• **National Unity Day Pledge**

questions.question: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), what was the proportion of population in multidimensional poverty (Headcount Ratio) in urban India in 2019-2021?

• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**

questions.question: A ______ happens in chess when a player gives up material during the initiation to seek some kind of compensation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gambit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A gambit in chess involves a player sacrificing material, usually a pawn, to gain a strategic advantage such as better positioning or initiative.
 
• The term "gambit" is derived from the Italian word "gambetto," meaning to trip someone.
 
• Common examples include the King’s Gambit and the Queen’s Gambit, which are well-known chess openings.
 
• Gambits can be accepted or declined by the opponent, leading to different lines of play.
 
• They are often used to surprise an opponent and force them into less familiar territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King’s Gambit**

 
 
• A historical chess opening starting with the moves 1.e4 e5 2.f4.
 
• It aims to control the center quickly and open lines for an aggressive attack.
 
• Popular during the 19th century, it is less common in modern high-level play due to its risky nature.
 
 
 
• **Queen’s Gambit**
 
 
• A classical chess opening starting with 1.d4 d5 2.c4.
 
• The objective is to offer the c4 pawn to gain a strong central presence.
 
• It is considered one of the most reliable and strategic openings in chess.
 
 
 
• **Accepted vs. Declined Gambits**
 
 
• In an accepted gambit, the opponent takes the offered material.
 
• In a declined gambit, the opponent avoids taking the material, instead focusing on other strategic goals.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Purpose**
 
 
• Gambits are used to disrupt the opponent’s plans and create dynamic positions.
 
• They often lead to complex and tactical middle games.

questions.question:

a. The Budget reflects the vision of the government in fulfilling the aspirations of people.

b. The Budget is the summary report of the financial performance of the government in power.

c. The Budget provides details of expenditures meted out by various Union Government ministries.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Government budget in India is a comprehensive financial statement that outlines the government's economic vision and policy priorities.
 
• It reflects the vision of the government in fulfilling the aspirations of the people by detailing plans for development and reforms (statement a).
 
• The Budget also serves as a summary report of the financial performance of the government in power, providing insights into revenue and expenditure (statement b).
 
• Furthermore, the Budget provides detailed accounts of expenditures incurred by various Union Government ministries and departments (statement c).
 
• The Union Budget is presented annually by the Finance Minister in Parliament and includes both revenue and capital budget estimates for the upcoming fiscal year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Budget**

 
 
• Comprises the government's revenue receipts (tax and non-tax revenues) and the expenditure met from these revenues.
 
• Revenue expenditures are those that do not result in the creation of assets, such as salaries, subsidies, and interest payments.
 
 
 
• **Capital Budget**
 
 
• Includes capital receipts (borrowings and disinvestments) and capital expenditures (outlays on asset creation like infrastructure).
 
• Capital expenditures are aimed at enhancing the productive capacity of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**
 
 
• It is the gap between total revenue and total expenditure of the government, excluding borrowings.
 
• A high fiscal deficit indicates the government is borrowing more to meet its expenses.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget Presentation**
 
 
• The Union Budget is presented by the Finance Minister in the Parliament, typically on February 1st each year.
 
• The budget covers the financial year, which runs from April 1 to March 31 of the following year.

questions.question: Kaal Baisakhi belongs to which state from the following?

__
 
• Kaal Baisakhi, also known as Nor'westers, is a local thunderstorm that occurs in the Indian state of **West Bengal**.
 
• These thunderstorms typically occur during the pre-monsoon season, from March to May.
 
• The storms are characterized by sudden, powerful winds, heavy rain, and occasionally hail.
 
• Kaal Baisakhi plays a crucial role in providing relief from the intense heat of the summer and in aiding the growth of crops like jute and paddy in West Bengal.

• The term "Kaal Baisakhi" is derived from the Bengali words "Kaal" meaning "fateful" and "Baisakhi" indicating the Bengali month of Baisakh (April-May).
 
 
 
• **Formation:**
 
 
• Kaal Baisakhi is formed due to the heating of the land, which causes the air to rise and form cumulonimbus clouds, leading to thunderstorms.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• While these storms are beneficial for agriculture, they can also cause significant damage to property, infrastructure, and can lead to fatalities.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Plastids?

options.text: Starch, oils and protein granules are stored in chromoplasts.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch, oils and protein granules are stored in chromoplasts.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chromoplasts are primarily involved in the synthesis and storage of pigments, particularly carotenoids, which give red, yellow, and orange colors to plant tissues.
 
• Plastids, including chromoplasts, have their own DNA and ribosomes, indicating their evolutionary origin from endosymbiotic bacteria.
 
• Chloroplasts, another type of plastid, contain stroma, which is a fluid matrix that houses the enzymes necessary for the synthesis of organic molecules during photosynthesis.
 
• Amyloplasts are the type of plastids that store starch, while elaioplasts store oils and proteinoplasts store proteins, not chromoplasts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroplasts:**

 
 
• These are the most well-known plastids and are responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells.
 
• They contain chlorophyll, the green pigment that captures light energy.
 
• The inner membrane of chloroplasts surrounds the stroma and thylakoid membranes where the light-dependent reactions occur.
 
 
 
• **Leucoplasts:**
 
 
• These are non-pigmented plastids found in non-photosynthetic tissues of plants, such as roots and seeds.
 
• They are involved in the synthesis and storage of starches, oils, and proteins.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory:**
 
 
• This theory suggests that plastids like chloroplasts and mitochondria originated from free-living bacteria that were engulfed by ancestral eukaryotic cells.
 
• The evidence supporting this theory includes the presence of their own DNA and ribosomes within these organelles.
 
 
 
• **Function of Stroma:**
 
 
• The stroma is the site of the Calvin cycle, where carbon dioxide is fixed into glucose using ATP and NADPH generated in the light-dependent reactions.
 
• It contains enzymes, ribosomes, and small circular DNA molecules.

• **Iron Age in India**

 
 
• The Iron Age in India began around 1500 BC and lasted until approximately 200 BC.
 
• This period is characterized by the widespread use of iron tools and weapons, which significantly enhanced agricultural productivity and warfare.
 
• Notable cultures from this period include the Painted Grey Ware culture and the Northern Black Polished Ware culture.

• **Gupta Period**

questions.question: From which of the following countries has the Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of the Concurrent List?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of Australia.
 
• The Concurrent List allows both the Union and the State Governments to legislate on certain matters.
 
• This list includes subjects like marriage, bankruptcy, trade unions, and education.
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws on a concurrent subject, the law made by the Union Government prevails.
 
• The inclusion of the Concurrent List ensures a balance of power and responsibilities between the central and state governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List**

 
 
• The Union List consists of subjects on which only the central government can legislate.
 
• It includes matters of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• There are 97 subjects listed under the Union List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **State List**
 
 
• The State List comprises subjects on which only the state governments can legislate.
 
• It includes matters of local or state importance such as police, public health, and agriculture.
 
• There are 66 subjects listed under the State List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Schedule**
 
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution outlines the division of powers between the Union and State governments.
 
• It contains three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• This schedule is crucial for maintaining the federal structure of India.
 
 
 
• **Residual Powers**
 
 
• Residual powers refer to subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists.
 
• According to the Indian Constitution, residual powers rest with the Union Government.
 
• This provision ensures that any new subject of legislation that arises is dealt with at the national level.

questions.question: __________ was launched by the Government of India in 2020 to make the country and its citizens independent and self-sufficient in all respects.

• The Abhiyan focuses on five main pillars: Economy, Infrastructure, System, Vibrant Demography, and Demand.
